### Array remove
 
-Use `Array.filter()` to find array elements that return truthy values and `Array.reduce()` to remove elements using `Array.splice()`.
-The `func` is invoked with three arguments (`value, index, array`).
+Finds elements that satisfy a predicate and returns them, at the same time modifying an original array.
+In other words, it works like [R#partition](http://ramdajs.com/docs/#partition), except that it mutates the original array and returns another partition instead of returning two.

Needs a note about literals:
```js
is(String, '') // false
is(Number, 1) // false
is(Boolean, true) // false
```

I've realized I can reduce this function to
```js
const getColonTimeFromDate = date => date.toTimeString().slice(0, 8)
```

```js
new Date().toTimeString() // "HH:MM:SS GMT 0000 (myTimeZone)"
getColonTimeFromDate(new Date()) // "HH:MM:SS"
```

Not sure if it's worth submitting at all.

Worth submitting IMHO; some don't realize one can just slice.
Keep in mind that many program JavaScript who are still novices; either new to programming or program other languages.  Having a copy/paste reference is handy!

When writing this PR I had thought to prefer building the colon string from independent values which would allow one to format the - if you wanted a 12 hour format. I imagined this function to be a higher function and formatting a single integer a lower function. To get the same result you'd need to format the result of this function which would not flow as nicely in practice.

I thought this PR would be a good reminder of some useful ways for using date, but #536 has convinced me of the need to act on one expected standard. Though it seems the project scope isn't in favor of handling these kinds of objects. If we were to submit these functions I feel my examples using regex patterns as discussed in #536 would be the best examples with the most value.
